quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: To choose what to do after thinking about options.
To accept that you are accountable for something that happened.
To complete a task by the required time.
To decide on something specific you want to achieve.

quests.hint: These four phrases describe positive habits that help someone succeed at work or in life.
quests.explanation: Set a goal comes first, giving you something to aim for, and make a decision is what you do repeatedly along the way. Meet a deadline adds a time limit to the mix, while take responsibility is about owning the outcome, good or bad, once it's done.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: A short, unannounced test given in class without advance notice.
Scheduled times when a teacher is available to meet students individually.
A formal warning given to a student whose grades are too low.
The time and effort needed to learn something new and challenging.

quests.hint: Each phrase describes a different part of student life, from testing to getting extra help.
quests.explanation: A pop quiz catches students off guard with no warning, while office hours give students a planned chance to get help instead. Academic probation is a serious warning about grades, and learning curve is different from all three — it simply describes how much effort a new skill takes to master.

quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: A formal meeting in which a manager assesses an employee's work.
Time off work given to a mother after the birth of a child.
The feeling of contentment a person has about their work.
The shared values, behaviors, and attitudes within an organization.

quests.hint: These phrases describe different sides of what it feels like to work somewhere.
quests.explanation: A performance review formally judges someone's work, while job satisfaction is about how that person personally feels about it. Maternity leave is a specific kind of time off, unrelated to either judgment or feeling, and workplace culture is the broadest term of all — the shared attitude of an entire organization.

quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: The process of converting one country's money into another.
A policy that covers costs if something goes wrong during a trip.
Describing a holiday package where all meals and activities are included.
The time of year when a destination receives the most visitors.

quests.hint: Each phrase relates to planning and paying for an overseas holiday.
quests.explanation: Currency exchange and travel insurance are both practical steps before a trip — one deals with money, the other with protection against problems. All-inclusive describes what's covered once you arrive, and peak season is unrelated to any of that; it simply describes timing, the busiest time of year to visit somewhere.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: Describing family members who no longer have a close relationship.
The main person in a family who earns the money to support others.
A family unit consisting of parents and their children only.
A family group including grandparents, aunts, uncles, and cousins.

quests.hint: These words describe different family structures and relationships.
quests.explanation: Nuclear family and extended family both describe the size of a family group, just at different scales — one is just parents and children, the other includes relatives further out. Breadwinner describes a role within that family, and estranged describes something else again — a relationship that has broken down.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: A store policy of lowering its price to match a competitor's lower price.
A very short sale offering large discounts for a limited time.
An offer that sells several products together at a lower total price.
Exchanging a used item as partial payment toward a new purchase.

quests.hint: Each phrase describes a different way to save money while shopping.
quests.explanation: A price match lowers a price to match a competitor, and a flash sale lowers it too, but only for a very short time. A bundle deal saves money differently, by combining products together, while a trade-in doesn't lower a price directly — it simply uses an old item as part of the payment.

quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: The tendency for people to underestimate how large their food portions are.
Food that has been significantly altered from its natural state.
Describing food that is naturally good for health and nutrition.
A type of fat found in animal products that can raise cholesterol levels.

quests.hint: Each phrase ties back to understanding what's actually on your plate.
quests.explanation: Wholesome and processed food sit at opposite ends of food quality — one is naturally good for you, the other has been heavily altered. Saturated fat is one specific thing to watch for within that food, and portion distortion is different from all three — it's about misjudging quantity, not quality.

quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: A service that allows data to be saved and accessed over the internet.
The visual design through which a user interacts with software or a device.
Software whose code is freely available for anyone to use or modify.
Using digital technology to harass, threaten, or bully someone.

quests.hint: These words all relate to using technology, for better or worse.
quests.explanation: Cloud storage and user interface are both about how software works — one about where data lives, the other about how you interact with it. Open source describes who can access and change that software, while cyberbullying is a completely different idea — the misuse of technology to harm someone.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: A medicine that kills or stops the growth of bacteria.
A substance that causes a loss of feeling or consciousness during a medical procedure.
Redness, swelling, and pain in part of the body as a reaction to injury or infection.
The force with which blood moves through the arteries.

quests.hint: Two of these are treatments, and two describe what's happening inside the body.
quests.explanation: An antibiotic and an anesthetic are both medical treatments, though one fights infection while the other blocks feeling during a procedure. Inflammation and blood pressure are different — they describe things happening inside the body itself, one a reaction to injury, the other a constant measurement.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: A book written by someone about their own life and experiences.
A collection of written works, such as poems or stories, by various authors.
A spoken or written account of connected events; a story.
Written language in its ordinary form, not poetry.

quests.hint: These words describe different forms writing can take.
quests.explanation: A memoir is one person's true story about their own life, while an anthology collects the work of many different authors. Narrative is broader than both — any account of connected events — and prose is broader still, simply meaning ordinary written language, as opposed to poetry.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: Behaving confidently and directly, clearly stating your needs and opinions.
Accepting situations without actively responding or defending oneself.
Careful and skillful in how you deal with people, avoiding offence.
Not clear or specific in meaning.

quests.hint: Each word describes a different style of communicating with others.
quests.explanation: Assertive and passive sit at opposite ends of communication — one states things directly, the other avoids doing so. Diplomatic takes a more careful path than either, avoiding offence while still communicating clearly. Vague is different from all three; it's not about a style at all, just a lack of clarity.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: Not having enough water in the body.
Not having enough of the right food for good health.
Describing a lifestyle involving little physical activity.
A medical condition in which excess body fat causes health problems.

quests.hint: Each word relates to a different way the body can be affected by diet or activity.
quests.explanation: Dehydrated is about water, and malnourished is about food quality, but both describe something the body lacks. Sedentary describes a lifestyle with little movement, and obesity is a medical condition that can result from patterns like that one, over time.

quests.instruction: Match each phrasal verb with its meaning.

pairs.value: To enter your username and password to access an account.
To register for a new account or service.
To move through content on a screen by sliding your finger or mouse.
When content spreads rapidly across the internet, reaching a large audience.

quests.hint: Picture using a social media app, from joining to watching something spread.
quests.explanation: Sign up happens once, creating an account, while log in happens every time afterward, just to access it. Scroll through is what you do once you're inside the app, and go viral is different from all three — it describes content itself spreading rapidly, not anything you personally do.

quests.instruction: Match each idiom with its meaning.

pairs.value: To do or say something to reduce tension or awkwardness at the start of a meeting.
To say the most important thing directly, without unnecessary detail.
To make sure a person is regularly updated about a situation.
To make brief contact with someone to check in or share information.

quests.hint: These phrases describe different habits of clear, considerate communication at work.
quests.explanation: Break the ice happens at the very start of a conversation, easing any awkwardness. Get to the point is nearly the opposite approach — skipping small talk entirely. Keep someone in the loop and touch base are both about staying connected over time, though touch base is usually a shorter, quicker check-in.

quests.instruction: Match each idiom with its meaning.

pairs.value: To begin studying seriously.
To stay awake all night to finish studying or work.
To perform extremely well on an exam.
To work or study until very late at night.

quests.hint: Picture the days before a big exam, right through to the result.
quests.explanation: Hit the books marks the start of serious studying, and burn the midnight oil describes doing that work very late at night. Pull an all-nighter takes it further still, staying awake the whole night, and ace a test is the hoped-for result of all that effort.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: The planned amount of money set aside to improve or repair a home.
An initial payment made when buying something expensive on credit.
A tax paid on the value of land or buildings owned.
The market value of a home minus any money still owed on it.

quests.hint: Every one of these phrases connects to the cost of owning and improving a home.
quests.explanation: A down payment is made when you first buy a home, and property tax is an ongoing cost you pay afterward simply for owning it. Renovation budget is money set aside for improvements later on, and home equity is different from all three — it's not a cost at all, but the value you've actually built up in the property.

quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: A form submitted to apply for financial support to pay for education.
A test taken to gain entry to a school, college, or program.
The student with the highest grades who gives a speech at graduation.
A sentence in an essay that summarizes the main argument.

quests.hint: Notice how each phrase connects to a different stage of a student's academic journey.
quests.explanation: An entrance exam and a scholarship application both happen before a student even starts, deciding who gets in and who gets funding. Valedictorian is an honor earned at the very end, at graduation, and thesis statement is unrelated to either — it's simply a sentence that summarizes the main argument of an essay.

quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: A legal agreement between a freelancer and a client defining the work and pay.
A document sent by a supplier requesting payment for goods or services.
A formal document listing work-related costs for reimbursement.
The difference between the selling price and the cost of producing something.

quests.hint: These phrases all tie back to money and paperwork in independent or business work.
quests.explanation: A freelance contract sets the terms of work before it begins, and an invoice requests payment once it's done. Expense report is a different kind of paperwork, listing costs to be reimbursed, and profit margin is different again — a calculation showing how much money is actually made after costs.

quests.instruction: Match each phrasal verb with its meaning.

pairs.value: To begin a new journey, project, or stage in life.
To get onto a plane, ship, or train to begin a journey.
To get off a ship, aircraft, or other vehicle.
To move forward toward a specific location, often used at airports.

quests.hint: These phrases follow the stages of a journey, from boarding to arriving.
quests.explanation: Embark on can describe starting any new journey or project, in a broad sense, while board is more specific — physically getting onto a plane, ship, or train. Proceed to is an instruction often heard at airports, guiding you somewhere next, and disembark is the very last step, getting off at the end.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: A short, personal story used to entertain or illustrate a point.
The art of using language persuasively and effectively.
Specialized words used by a particular group that others may not understand.
To express what someone else said using different words.

quests.hint: Each word relates to a different way language can be used or reshaped.
quests.explanation: An anecdote is a short personal story used to make a point, while rhetoric is the broader skill of using language persuasively in general. Jargon is language limited to one particular group, and paraphrase is different from all three — it's the act of restating someone else's words in your own.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: Influence from people your own age to behave in a certain way.
A person others admire and try to copy in behavior or lifestyle.
Competition or jealousy between brothers or sisters.
The sadness parents feel when all their children have left home.

quests.hint: Each phrase describes a different kind of influence or emotion within family and friendships.
quests.explanation: Peer pressure comes from friends your own age, while a role model is someone you look up to and copy, often older. Sibling rivalry is competition between brothers or sisters, and empty nest syndrome is different from all three — the sadness parents feel once their children have grown up and moved away.

quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: A pass allowing repeated access to events or transport over a set period.
A person or company that sells goods or services.
To argue about or negotiate the price of something.
A purchase made without planning, based on a sudden urge.

quests.hint: Each of these phrases points to a different moment in buying or selling something.
quests.explanation: A vendor is the person selling, and to haggle is something a buyer might do with that vendor to lower the price. A season ticket is a planned, repeated purchase, and an impulse buy is nearly the opposite — a sudden purchase made with no planning at all.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: Describing food with a strong, hot flavor from chili or similar spices.
Describing a strong, pleasant taste that is not sweet.
Describing food with very little taste or flavor.
Describing a sharp, slightly sour or acidic taste.

quests.hint: Each word describes a different taste you might notice while eating.
quests.explanation: Spicy brings heat from chili or similar spices, while savory is a rich, non-sweet flavor without any heat involved. Bland sits at the opposite end from both — very little flavor at all — and tangy is a sharper taste, slightly sour or acidic.

quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: The total amount of time a person spends using a screen each day.
A period of time spent away from electronic devices deliberately.
Electronic devices worn on the body, such as smartwatches.
A person with many online followers whose opinions affect others.

quests.hint: These phrases all relate to how technology fits into daily life.
quests.explanation: Screen time measures how long you use a screen, while a digital detox is the opposite choice — deliberately stepping away from devices. Wearable technology is a type of device itself, worn on the body, and a social media influencer is different from all three — a person, not a habit or a device.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: Basic emergency care given to an injured person before medical help arrives.
An emergency technique that keeps blood circulating when the heart stops.
Keeping a person or animal apart from others to prevent spreading illness.
A process of recovery that helps a person regain health or function.

quests.hint: Each phrase relates to a different stage of responding to illness or injury.
quests.explanation: First aid and CPR are both immediate responses to an emergency, though CPR is specifically used when the heart stops. Quarantine is a preventive step, keeping illness from spreading to others, and rehabilitation comes much later — the longer process of recovering health or function.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: A performance in which a comedian tells jokes to a live audience.
To create or perform something without preparation or a script.
The group of actors in a film, show, or play.
The written text of what will be said and done in a film or show.

quests.hint: Each word relates to a different part of putting on a live or filmed performance.
quests.explanation: A script is written in advance, laying out what will be said, while to improvise means performing without one. Stand-up comedy often relies on both skills at once, and cast is different from all three — it's simply the group of actors performing, not a skill or a document.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: A style of language used in official, professional, or polite situations.
A casual, relaxed style of language used with friends or family.
Very informal words or phrases used by a particular group.
A shortened form of a word or phrase.

quests.hint: These words describe different styles you might notice while reading or listening to English.
quests.explanation: Formal and informal register sit at opposite ends of tone — one is used in professional settings, the other with friends and family. Slang belongs mostly to informal register, understood only by certain groups, and abbreviation is different from all three — simply a shortened form of a word, used in any style.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: An important discovery or achievement that solves a difficult problem.
A standard or reference point used to measure or compare performance.
The quality of being practical or possible to achieve.
An early version of a product built to test a concept.

quests.hint: Each word relates to a different stage of developing something new.
quests.explanation: Feasibility is checked first, before any real work begins, to see if an idea is even possible. A prototype comes next, an early version built to test that idea, and a breakthrough is the exciting result if it truly works. Benchmark is different from all three — a standard used to measure and compare progress, at any stage.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: Preferring to spend time alone rather than in groups; quiet and reserved.
Preferring to be around people and gaining energy from social activities.
Having mixed or uncertain feelings about something.
Able to recover quickly from difficulties or challenges.

quests.hint: Each word describes a different personality trait or emotional response.
quests.explanation: Introverted and extroverted are opposites, describing whether someone prefers solitude or company. Ambivalent describes uncertainty rather than a fixed personality trait, and resilient is different from all three — it's about bouncing back from difficulty, not about personality type at all.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: The price paid to use public transport such as a bus or train.
A list of scheduled times for transport or events.
The planned path taken to travel from one place to another.
A raised area beside a railway track where passengers board trains.

quests.hint: Each word relates to using public transport, from planning to boarding.
quests.explanation: A timetable tells you when transport runs, and a route tells you the path it follows. Fare is the price you pay to use it, and platform is different from all three — the physical place beside the tracks where you actually board the train.
